newsitem.title: FRANCE: Slovakia's political record harms EU entry plan.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia's political record harms EU entry plan.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday Slovakia's record on political reforms had ruled it out of the first wave of European Union membership talks.

Although the Commission said most of 10 eastern European applicants' political systems were found wanting in some way, only in Slovakia was the political situation bad enough to affect its EU membership plans.

"The opinions conclude that, although the quality of democracy could be further improved in most countries, only in Slovakia are political problems sufficiently severe as to rule out in themselves negotiations," the EU's External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek told the European Parliament.
The Commission on Wednesday recommended that the EU open membership talks early next year with Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Estonia and Slovenia, along with Cyprus.
Slovakia, Latvia, Lithuania, Bulgaria and Romania were not yet ready, it said.

Van den Broek, echoing a regular theme of meetings with the Slovak authorities over the past few months, told the parliament the EU executive's main concern was the lack of stability of Slovakia's political institutions.
He said it was the job of those institutions to guarantee democracy and respect for human rights and minorities.
Commission President Jacques Santer, questioned by Slovak reporters during a news conference, refused to comment by name on Slovakia's hardline Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar.
But Van den Broek told reporters he had raised the problems during a recent meeting with Meciar.
The Commission assessment says that the government pays insufficient respect to the powers devolved by the constitution to other bodies and "too frequenty disregards the rights of the opposition."
It also cites the way the government recently ignored decisions by the Constitutional Court and the central referendum committee on voting on May 23-24.
Slovaks went to the polls in plebiscites on NATO membership and direct presidential elections but the votes were declared void because ballot papers were invalid.
The referendum committee declared the widely boycotted poll void and denounced ballot papers distributed by the interior ministry as a "massive swindle".
It also underlined concerns about government use of the police and the secret services and lack of independence of the judicial system.
The Commission says that on economic grounds Slovakia could satisfy the conditions set by the EU for membership in the medium term.
